key: But I have three precious things which I prize and hold fast. The first is gentleness; the second is economy; and the third is shrinking from taking precedence of others.
s: After answering what the world says of the speaker’s Tao, the chapter names his treasures; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 67, reads the three as loving the people like infants, taxing as though taking from oneself, and keeping humble, never first to begin.

evidence.words: 愛百姓若赤子。…賦歛若取之於己也。…執謙退，不為倡始也。
evidence.gloss: (On gentleness:) loving the hundred clans as newborn infants. (On economy:) levying taxes as though taking them from oneself. (On not daring to be first:) holding to humility and withdrawal, not being the one who starts things.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 67, at [66]). The Heshang Gong commentary glosses each of the three treasures on its own line: 慈 as loving the people as infants, 儉 as taxing as though taking from oneself, 不敢為天下先 as holding to humility and not initiating. The sentence carries exactly these three glosses; Wang Bi’s comment on the same lines treats their effects, not their content. Plain sense (the chapter answers what the world says of its Tao, then names the treasures) is faithful and repeats no four words of the key. entry-check ok, 44 words.
